meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (national unitary jurisdiction; nine provinces with no materially distinct corporate sub-state regime)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch civil-law foundation overlain by English common law, constitutional supremacy and African customary law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Protection of Investment Act 22 of 2015 (unilateral statutory investment-protection framework; legacy bilateral investment treaties largely terminated or under renegotiation)
Double Taxation Agreements with the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, China, Japan, India, Mauritius, Kenya, Nigeria and Botswana
African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008 as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 (beneficial-ownership register provisions effective 1 April 2023) and the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; Companies Regulations 2011 (as amended); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 as amended by the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act 1 of 2017; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; FIC Guidance Notes and Directives on beneficial ownership, customer due diligence and politically exposed persons.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner's valid passport (notarially certified by a notary public in the country of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's country of residence (e.g. Japan or China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (South Africa is a Contracting State to the Hague Apostille Convention since 1995; foreign public documents must be apostilled by the competent authority of the country of origin; no consular legalization is required for Hague-member source states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within the immediately preceding three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or banking institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the competent authority of the country of origin; notarially certified copy annexed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation (account history and relationship report issued by the UBO's home bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent banking institution of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the competent authority of the country of origin; notarially certified copy annexed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised Foreign Certificate of Incorporation and good-standing extract (required where the shareholder is a foreign corporate entity rather than an individual)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or companies office of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the competent authority of the jurisdiction of incorporation; consular legalization through the South African embassy only for non-Hague-member jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised UBO declaration and beneficial-ownership disclosure schedule (statutory declaration submitted to the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission for the CIPC beneficial-ownership register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South African notary public or commissioner of oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for domestic South African notarisation; filing accompanies the incorporation submission via the CIPC bizeReg portal

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, proposed directors, shareholders and beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the South African domestic designations list administered under POCDATARA, the OFAC SDN list (required for USD correspondent clearing via Swift_TT), and the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists where EUR or GBP payment rails are used. PEP status must be determined for both domestic and foreign politically exposed persons in accordance with FIC guidance; any positive PEP or sanctions hit requires enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval prior to incorporation. Continuous adverse-media screening is mandated for the duration of the bank account relationship.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.banking_aml_risk_tier_assessment: Low_Risk_Standard (non-accountable-institution wholesale food distributor; standard customer due diligence applies at the designated bank; no automatic enhanced due diligence triggers absent PEP or sanctions findings)

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC bizeReg e-services portal of the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (https://eservices.cipc.co.za); name reservation submitted on Form CoR 9.1
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin (Roman) script using the letters, digits and punctuation permitted by the Companies Regulations 2011. Any of South Africa's eleven official languages may be used, but the name must be readily transliteratable into Latin characters. The proposed name 'ZA Matcha (Pty) Ltd' is in English script and satisfies the transliteration doctrine. Foreign-script or non-official-language expressions and names with numerals in unusual positions require CIPC adjudication.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A CIPC name rejection is deliverable electronically through bizeReg with the statutory ground stated (typically confusing similarity under s 11(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008). Appeal and remedy pathway: (i) lodge a written complaint with the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act within 10 business days of the rejection notice; (ii) simultaneously or alternatively file a fresh CoR 9.1 name-reservation application containing a distinguishing prefix or geographic qualifier; (iii) where the objection rests on a third-party registered name or trademark, procure a letter of consent and re-file; or (iv) incorporate using the company registration number as a transitional name and subsequently apply for a s 160 name change once the disputed mark is cleared. A reserved name may be renewed once for a further six months by filing a renewal application before expiry of the initial reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_mandate_detail: Section 23(2) and s 23(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 require every company to continuously maintain a registered office at a physical address in South Africa, which must not be a post-office box, and at which the company's statutory records are capable of being inspected and process may be served.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible_with_Conditions: a virtual or serviced office is acceptable for a low-risk wholesale distribution company such as the proposed matcha trader, provided the address is a genuine physical South African location where records are accessible and service of process can be accepted. The CIPC-registered office may differ from the operational warehouse or customs-bonded facility. A pure virtual address without record-keeping and process-acceptance capacity is not permissible, and regulated financial activities would never qualify.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk 8–15% within the first 12 months. CIPC does not conduct routine physical substance inspections for low-risk wholesale food distributors; however, site-comprehension checks may occur through SARS customs and VAT desk interventions, the Department of Agriculture food-import verification, or the designating bank's FICA-driven continuous due diligence. Any discrepancy between the registered office and actual trading premises will heighten the inspection probability and AML risk classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 13 (Incorporation), 14 (Registration), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (Legal personality), 21 (Change of name), 26 (Share register), 40 (Issue of shares), 66 (Board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) read with the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A/B) filed through the CIPC e-Services portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; the company must have at least one issued share. Share capital can be authorised at a nominal aggregate value, and no escrow account or capital deposit is required for a private company incorporated in South Africa.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the allotment of 1,000 ordinary shares at R1.00 per share to the subscribers is approved and recorded; (2) the registered office stated in the Notice of Incorporation is adopted as the Company's official statutory address; (3) [Director A] and [Director B] are appointed as directors, and [Company Secretary] is appointed as company secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or removal under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; (4) the directors are authorised to open bank accounts, file tax registrations, execute all ancillary documents, and do all things necessary to give full effect to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and directors due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC e-Services portal and complete the CoR 9.1 application for name reservation, or elect to incorporate under a registered company number where a trade name is not essential. Verify that the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name or trade mark. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee electronically and download the acknowledgment notice.
required_dossiers: Completed CoR 9.1 name reservation application
Proposed company name or election to use registered number
Identity documents or passports of the proposed incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a fresh CoR 9.1 application with alternative name options within 10 business days, or lodge a formal objection/appeal within the time limits prescribed under section 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC – Companies Registration Section, e-Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and upload the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation and signed consent to act as director. Submit the bundle through the CIPC e-Services portal, pay the Rand-denominated filing fee, and await the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation with a company registration number.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A/B)
Consent to Act as Director forms
Identity documents or passports of directors
Proof of name reservation reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or rejection, correct the flagged fields and resubmit electronically within 10 business days; attach explanatory notes and pay the resubmission fee where applicable. Continue the incorporation by complying with CIPC's revised compliance notes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: South African Revenue Service tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling and regional branch office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated private company for income tax, value-added tax if annual taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed the registration threshold, PAYE withholding if employees are hired, and customs code registration for the cross-border import and export of matcha powder. Submit the company registration Certificate and supporting documents to obtain the tax reference number and customs importer/exporter code.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
Directors' identity documents
Company bank confirmation or account details where available
SARS ITREG application forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS may issue a notice requesting additional documentary proof or a letter of finalisation; respond within 30 days with the missing corporate records and confirm compliance with the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered office adoption and statutory corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC and company secretary/registered officer of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the registered office as indicated in the Notice of Incorporation and maintain the statutory records required under the Companies Act, including the minute book, share register, register of directors, and beneficial ownership register. If the public interest score so requires, appoint an independent reviewer or auditor within 40 business days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
Fixed office address proof, such as lease agreement or title deed
Directors' service contracts and consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return filing date is imminent, file the first annual return in the ordinary course; if CIPC detects a lapse in record-keeping, submit a rectification filing and pay any prescribed late-filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial bank account and cross-border payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African commercial bank, financial crimes compliance department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the registered company name, presenting the Board Resolution, Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation, directors' identities, and entity beneficial ownership attestation. Configure the account for SWIFT TT inward and outward remittances to support the matcha powder trade.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution authorising account opening
CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum of Incorporation
Passport/ID copies of all directors and beneficial owners
Proof of registered office and physical trading address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the beneficial ownership structure under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, submit an updated group org chart, declaration of beneficial owners, and certified credentials for each signatory.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership filing and annual compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC – Beneficial Ownership Register and Compliance Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory deadlines after incorporation, file the beneficial ownership particulars with CIPC and thereafter on any change. Calendar the annual return date and maintain a complete register of shareholders and beneficial owners as required by the Companies Act and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022.
required_dossiers: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation
Beneficial ownership schedule identifying natural persons with control
Directors' and beneficial owners' identity documents
Company register of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing is queried, resubmit the corrected schedule with supporting attestations. For late annual returns, pay the prescribed penalty and file the outstanding annual return through CIPC e-Services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) – no sectoral industrial licence is triggered for a pure wholesale trading business in culinary and ceremonial grade matcha powder under ISIC 4631 / NAICS 424490
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate operating or manufacturing licence is required; the company must however obtain an SARS customs importer/exporter code and, where applicable, a municipal business registration or trading certificate for its office and warehouse.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and local municipal environmental health authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration only – no listed activity under the EIA Regulations, 2014 (GN 983/984) for warehouse distribution of packaged matcha powder; a full EIA report would only be triggered if the company later establishes industrial processing, milling or agro-processing activities involving listed effluent or emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or atmospheric emission is expected. Sanitary effluent must meet municipal sewer by-law standards. Food-grade matcha powder must be stored in airtight, moisture-resistant containers below 25°C and below 60% relative humidity. Any dangerous waste, if generated, must be handled and disposed in compliance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance must be certified by the local accredited fire protection services; the workplace must comply with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including electrical installation certificates and first-aid readiness. A Certificate of Occupancy from the local municipality is required for the registered office and warehouse. If the company repacks or re-labels matcha, implement a documented food-safety management system aligned with HACCP principles.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a South African income tax reference number and VAT registration through SARS eFiling. Required supporting documents include CIPC company registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, foreign passport/national ID of directors, proof of physical address, bank account details, and a letter appointing a registered representative taxpayer in South Africa. Applications are submitted online, and the tax/VAT registration number is issued once SARS validates the entity's local substance and commercial presence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box system. A (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily taxed at entity level as a resident company. Limited elections are available for small businesses under Turnover Tax (s6 Income Tax Act) and for group relief arrangements; hybrid mismatch rules under s25G and s25H restrict certain cross-border structured transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 compulsory taxable turnover threshold; R50,000 voluntary registration threshold for input recovery
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. VAT invoices must contain SARS-specified particulars and be issued within 21 days of supply. E-invoicing is permitted under the SARS eFiling/E-invoice framework using standard XML/UBL formats, and taxpayers must retain transactional data and support an electronic data interchange for SARS audit requests.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of matcha powder qualifies for zero-rating under Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act when goods are supplied to a non-resident, are exported from South Africa within a prescribed period (generally 60 days from date of supply unless extended), and documentary proof of physical export is retained. Related offshore services are zero-rated under Section 11(2)(k) where supplied to non-residents for direct export purposes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS conducts post-clearance and desk audits requiring verification of actual physical export, customs declarations, transport documents, and foreign-currency payment receipts. Failure to substantiate zero-rating triggers a VAT assessment at 15% on the export value, plus understatement penalties (up to 200%) and prescribed interest. Fraudulent or deliberately false zero-rating claims constitute a criminal offence punishable by fines, imprisonment, and retrospective clawback of all attributed VAT refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the Exchange Control authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), with AML/CFT supervision by the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) and prudential regulation by the SARB-subsidiary Prudential Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The rand is fully convertible for all bona fide current-account transactions, including the importation of organic matcha powder (HS 0902.10), freight, insurance, commissions and service fees, subject to documentary verification by an authorised dealer under the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers (CMAD). Capital-account convertibility is managed: inward foreign equity investments by non-residents are freely permitted and require reporting (not pre-approval) through the authorised dealer's Balance of Payments (BOP) system; repayment of shareholder loans below the FinSurv materiality threshold (ZAR 100 million equivalent) is permitted on registration, while larger borrowings require prior FinSurv approval. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders require no FinSurv approval provided the underlying equity was sourced from genuinely foreign capital, the company possesses a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin, audited or independently reviewed financial statements are submitted, the dividend was declared in compliance with the Companies Act, and South African dividends tax at 20% (or lower treaty rate on a valid DTA declaration) is withheld and paid to SARS. The company must also maintain OECD-compliant transfer-pricing documentation for any intra-group payables to prevent thin-capitalisation or recharacterisation adjustments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Circular 09/2021 and the CMAD export chapter, proceeds from exports of goods must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment; the former mandatory 50% conversion of export proceeds into rand is abolished, and the effective surrender ratio is 0% provided 100% of each receipt is repatriated into a South African account or an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) maintained with an authorised dealer. The exporter must submit an exporting-form-validated SAD500 Customs export declaration, obtain a SARS Customs client code and Export Clearing Number, quote the bill of lading or airway bill, and close out each shipment within the 180-day window; failure to do so creates an Unremitted Export Proceeds (UEP) flag, requiring FinSurv extension approval, and can trigger suspension of the company's import/export trade facility with the bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR Account, Foreign Currency Account (USD/JPY/CNY), Capital Escrow Account facility, Trade Finance and Documentary Credits

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank - FNB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Business Account with integrated eFX and FNB Corporate Trade module, Foreign Currency Account
Operational Current Account, Capital Escrow Account, Import/Export Trade and Working Capital facility
Operational Account and Foreign Currency Account, dedicated Agriculture/FMCG sector trade desk, Commercial LC and Trust Receipt facilities
Premium Operational Account, Private Treasury and Capital Escrow Account for structured inward investment
Basic Business Transactional Account only; no full cross-border trade finance or LC capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Onshore neobanks such as TymeBank and Bank Zero are licensed banks under the Banks Act 94 of 1990 but do not presently offer documentary collections, letters of credit, SARB BOP registration or FCA-based treasury rails suitable for a cross-border matcha importer. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Payoneer) are neither licensed banks nor authorised dealers in South Africa; under the Banks Act and the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 they cannot open an account in the name of a South African company at their own balance sheet and cannot perform Exchange Control reporting or FICA CDD on behalf of the regulated bank. Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury rail; Medium as a supplementary collection or supplier-disbursement side rail for low-value payments in USD/EUR/JPY corridors, provided every transaction is mirrored in the primary bank's KYC file and the regulated bank remains the source of BOP/FinSurv reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The amended Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA), read with the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and FIC Guidance Note 5A, permits non-face-to-face verification where reliable independent electronic data sources are used, so a fully remote opening is legally possible. In practice, Standard Bank, FNB, Absa and Nedbank require at least one natural-person director with a South African ID or a valid business/visa permit to appear either physically at a branch or through an approved live-video KYC session with two compliance officers; where the entire board is non-resident, banks mandate notarised and apostilled passports of all directors, a good-standing reference from each director's foreign regulated bank, a physical registered office in the Republic, and a signed resolution appointing a South African authorised representative for bank liaison. Onboarding timelines of 5 to 15 business days should be budgeted; full non-resident opening without any local director is generally declined or restricted to a transaction-based account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners (BOs) and a board without South African residence, creating heightened source-of-funds and footprint uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FIC-compliant Beneficial Ownership register identifying every person with 25% or more ownership or control; CIPC Beneficial Ownership filing confirmation; notarised and apostilled passports and proof of residential address for all directors and significant shareholders; foreign tax identification numbers; three-year bank statements and regulated-bank reference letters for each BO; independent sanctions and adverse-media screening report (World-Check/Refinitiv) showing no hits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of funds and source of wealth for the initial capital injection and the matcha purchase programme.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month source-of-funds bank statements, investor wealth statement or audited balance sheet, executed equity subscription or loan agreement, board resolution approving the funding, SWIFT evidence that funds were debited from the remitter's own account, and a written trade-cycle narrative covering advance payments versus documentary credit to matcha suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SARS tax compliance gaps, unregistered VAT status or absence of Customs import/export codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin for the company and directors, VAT registration under category B, SARS Customs client codes for import and export, latest Companies Act annual return, CIPC certificate of incorporation, and a records-management plan showing segregation of cross-border invoicing from domestic supply.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions false positives, adverse media or trade-corridor scrutiny relating to East Asian suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial narrative letter, signed purchase orders and proforma invoices on Incoterms basis, HS 0902.10 classification memorandum, organic certification certificates (Ceres, USDA Organic, EU Organic) proving food-grade and non-dual-use nature, bill-of-lading and chain-of-custody evidence, plus any FIC section 35(4) disclosure if a discrepancy arises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through trust, nominee or intermediate holding structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trust deed or nominee declaration extract, declaration by the corporate service provider as to nominal ownership, CIPC registry screenshot of persons of significant control, shareholder register and MOI share-class schedule, and confirmation that each intermediate entity is a pure holding special-purpose vehicle with published directors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder equity injection: the shareholder must remit from its own foreign bank account via SWIFT MT103, with ordering-customer field 50K matching the name on the shareholder register and field 72 stating 'Inward Foreign Investment - Equity Subscription'; the funds are credited to the (Pty) Ltd operational ZAR or multi-currency account at the authorised dealer, which captures the receipt in SARB's Balance of Payments system (the former Form N modality, now electronically reported) and issues a BOP transaction reference for the company's records. The company must file the Companies Act allotment return, keep the share subscription agreement, board resolution and payment instruction, and ensure no round-tripping or loop structure exists in which South African funds leave and re-enter as purported foreign capital. Shareholder loans follow the same routing and are registered as BOP loans; loans above ZAR 100 million equivalent require prior FinSurv approval and a signed facility agreement with market-conforming interest rates to avoid thin-capitalisation. A Capital Escrow Account is not statutorily required for pure equity, but is recommended at Absa or Standard Bank where proceeds must be held pending supplier contract effectiveness or Customs registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Import disbursements for matcha: the company presents the supplier invoice, insurance document and transport evidence (airway bill or bill of lading) and, for customs-cleared shipments, the SAD500 Bill of Entry; the authorised dealer converts ZAR to JPY, CNY or USD and releases payment via SWIFT MT103 through the correspondent network. For deferred supplier terms, a commercial letter of credit is established by the South African issuing bank via SWIFT MT700, with settlement against compliant presentation (commercial invoice, packing list, B/L, organic certificates) under SWIFT MT202 COV bank-to-bank reimbursement, while the ZAR funding leg is settled through SARB's SAMOS real-time gross settlement system. All import payments must be completed within 180 days of shipment; late settlement triggers an 'Unpaid Import' (UPI) report to FinSurv and may require prior approval. Recommended infrastructure: Standard Bank or FNB trade finance modules, SWIFT gpi for end-to-end tracking, and a USD Foreign Currency Account to pre-fund suppliers and reduce conversion slippage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) up to 12 months, bookable with any authorised dealer against documented current-account trade exposure, with no FinSurv approval required
FX Swap (spot-forward or forward-forward) to restructure cash-flow dates on existing import/export payment obligations
Vanilla FX Options and Zero-Cost Collars covering notional amounts equal to underlying purchase orders and supplier invoices
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) for long-term foreign-currency funding or capital transactions approved by FinSurv

Roll-over and early termination of FECs at prevailing market rates, provided no speculative position is created; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore as the rand is fully deliverable, and hedging must be executed as deliverable contracts with the authorised dealer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 days of the anniversary month of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late penalty of up to ZAR 500 (approx. USD 27) for overdue filing; two consecutive years of non-filing triggers administrative deregistration after formal CIPC notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of registration anniversary, and quarterly if no change; updated within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compliance notice followed by a fine up to ZAR 100,000 (approx. USD 5,400) per non-compliance instance under the Companies Act; continued non-compliance may result in deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the company's financial year-end (unless an extension is approved)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% per-month penalty on outstanding assessed tax for late filing, plus prescribed SARS interest; persistent non-compliance can lead to criminal prosecution of the responsible directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Distribution (if required by articles or affected entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; lodged at CIPC only where required by the Companies Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end for member distribution; CIPC filing of AFS applies only when mandatory (e.g., PIS ≥ 100 or foreign-controlled company threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors in default may be held civilly liable; administrative penalties of up to ZAR 50,000 (approx. USD 2,700) may be imposed by the Companies Tribunal for non-compliance with AFS obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required if the public interest score (PIS) equals or exceeds 350. For a private company with PIS between 100 and 349, an independent review by a registered accountant is required; audit exemption applies when PIS < 100. As a low-risk wholesale trader with PIS below 100, the company qualifies for audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, IFRS for SMEs, or a standard prescribed by the Minister of Justice and Corporate/Commerce under Section 29 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must submit a beneficial ownership confirmation with CIPC within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary and within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership. Share transfer forms must be lodged with CIPC, and the statutory beneficial ownership register must be updated simultaneously. Failure to do so is a non-compliance offence under the Companies Act and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for PIS < 100; if triggered, 2,500 - 4,300

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for all resident companies for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad-based tax holiday. Qualifying Small Business Corporations (SBCs) with gross income not exceeding R20 million enjoy a graduated rate scale (0% to 27%). Section 11D research & development deduction, Section 12B renewable energy allowance, and Section 12E accelerated depreciation for SBCs are available where applicable. Assessed losses are carried forward indefinitely subject to the continuity of ownership and trade rules in Section 20A of the Income Tax Act (the numeric limit of -1 is used to denote 'no fixed statutory term limit').

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically through SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be submitted within 12 months after the end of the company’s financial year (year of assessment). SARS may issue a notice accelerating the filing date; in practice, the deadline is the last business day of the 12th month following the year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registration number, trading name, and postal/physical address registered with CIPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name and registration number of the South African Pty Ltd. Disclose the non-resident ultimate beneficial owner and shareholding percentage in the related ownership schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date on which the financial year ends (e.g., 28 February).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same year-end as registered with SARS for provisional tax deadlines. A short first-year return may be filed if the company has not previously reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales proceeds derived from the distribution of culinary and ceremonial grade matcha powder, excluding VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only South African-source income and foreign trade income attributable to the local operations. Ensure that any income already subjected to foreign tax is separately disclosed in the foreign tax credit schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenditure incurred in the production of gross income: cost of imported matcha, freight and shipping, customs duties, warehousing, advertising, salaries, rent, insurance, and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be supported by sufficient invoices and paid/proven to be for the benefit of the South African entity. Circular cross-border payments to related foreign suppliers must meet arm's-length transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as gross income less allowable deductions less any assessed loss brought forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company has a previously assessed loss, the section 20A continuity-of-ownership and continuity-of-trade tests must be satisfied to utilise that loss against current-year income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 27% corporate rate (or SBC graduated rates) to taxable income; subtract rebates and prepaid provisional tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the effective tax on the taxable income. Foreign dividends and passive foreign income may qualify for exemptions (e.g., section 10B or participation exemption).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year assessed loss carried into the current year and applied against current income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the section 20A schedule demonstrating that the same trade was continued and equity ownership did not significantly change within the applicable six-year rolling window.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of all dividends during the year, including dividends to non-resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the amount of dividends paid and any dividends tax withheld at source for each non-resident shareholder, referencing the treaty rate applied and the basis for relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the ITR14 attracts an administrative non-compliance penalty of up to R250 per month or part of a month for each month of non-compliance, capped at R4,000 per tax year. The late payment of corporate income tax results in a 10% late-payment penalty on the unpaid amount plus statutory interest at the prescribed rate (currently over 10% per annum). If the return is subject to an understatement, penalties range from 0% to 200% of the understated tax depending on the taxpayer’s conduct (e.g., substantial non-compliance, gross negligence, or fraud).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 – Provisional Tax Return, filed through SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual (two compulsory provisional payments; a third voluntary payment is permitted)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional tax payment: last day of the sixth month of the year of assessment (e.g., 31 August for a February year-end). Second provisional tax payment: the last day of the year of assessment (e.g., 28/29 February for a February year-end). Third voluntary payment: within six months after the end of the year of assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimate of total taxable income for the year of assessment, based on the latest available financial and trading information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include South African-source income and profits attributable to the local permanent establishment. If the company is in its first year, estimate based on realistic monthly projections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of tax due for the current provisional period, calculated at 27% (or SBC rates) on the estimated taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The first payment must not be less than 50% of the final tax liability, and the second payment must bring the total to 100% of the final liability unless a minimum estimate is used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid provisional tax amounts already paid for the year, which are set off against the final ITR14 liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile these amounts with the IRP6 payment history and ensure foreign tax credits are properly claimed before arriving at the net liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of provisional tax triggers an interest charge at the prescribed rate on the shortfall from the original due date. Administrative penalties for late filing of the IRP6 may be imposed at the same monthly rate of up to R250 per month, capped at R4,000 per tax year. A taxpayer who deliberately submits a grossly inaccurate estimate may face a 200% understatement penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final dividend withholding tax on dividends declared by a South African resident company to non-resident beneficial owners, effective for dividends paid on or after 22 February 2017.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the South African paying company (or the authorised agent) before payment: (i) a completed Declaration / DT form (South African Revenue Service form) confirming beneficial ownership and eligibility for treaty relief, and (ii) an original or certified copy of the tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign revenue authority. The South African company then withholds at the treaty rate, commonly 5% for corporate holdings of 10% or more and 10%–15% for other holdings. If the documentation is not provided, the statutory 20% rate applies. Over-withheld amounts may be recovered by the non-resident through a formal refund application with SARS, supported by the same documentation and an IT3(a) dividend certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory final withholding tax of 15% is imposed on gross royalties paid from a South African source to a non-resident for the use of or the right to use intellectual property. Most DTAs reduce the royalty withholding rate to between 0% and 10%, depending on the type of IP and the DTA partner. Interest: a 15% final withholding tax applies to interest from a South African source paid to non-residents unless an exemption applies (e.g., interest on certain listed debt instruments or interest paid to a non-resident beneficial owner not effectively connected to a PE). Many DTAs reduce or eliminate the interest withholding tax (e.g., 0% for beneficial owners under the US-SA and UK-SA treaties, subject to specific conditions). To claim treaty relief, the non-resident must provide the required declaration and TRC to the South African payor before the payment is made.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold is prescribed in the Income Tax Act or Tax Administration Act. SARS requires taxpayers to prepare and retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) for all cross-border transactions with connected persons. In SARS administrative guidance, a full transfer-pricing analysis has historically been expected for affected transactions exceeding R5 million in annual value, but in all cases the documentation must be sufficient to demonstrate that the pricing is consistent with the arm's length principle.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as found in the UAE or Cayman Islands. However, economic substance is central to the tax residence determination (place of effective management) and to the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in section 80A-L of the Income Tax Act. A company that is formally a South African resident but lacks genuine commercial activity, full-time employees, local decision-making, or real business premises may be re-characterised as a shell or conduit arrangement. SARS will then disregard the legal form, allocate income to the jurisdiction where economic activities are performed, and deny treaty benefits. The same anti-avoidance principles, combined with controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution rules in section 9D, prevent passive income from being shifted to low-tax jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cross-border matcha sales revenue from the ITR14, fabricating expenses, or submitting false customs and VAT documentation to SARS in order to understate taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty under section 104 of the Income Tax Act: a fine of up to R10,000 and/or imprisonment for a period not exceeding five years. In addition, SARS may impose an administrative understatement penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall plus statutory interest. The individual and the company can be prosecuted simultaneously.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in or authorise tax evasion may be prosecuted as co-principals; they may also be held personally liable for the company's unpaid tax debt under section 237 of the Tax Administration Act, which includes civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a South African Pty Ltd with no physical office, no local employees, and no substantive commercial activity, using it solely as a pass-through to route income to foreign shareholders or to claim DTA benefits without genuine economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may apply the general anti-avoidance rule (section 80A-L) to disregard the transaction, reallocate the income to the shareholder or foreign parent, deny treaty benefits, and impose an understatement penalty of up to 200% of the tax assessed. The company may also lose its tax residence status if its place of effective management is outside South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who established or operated the shell arrangement may be personally liable for the additional tax, penalties, and interest. Courts may impose a civil order for restitution equal to the tax shortfall, issue travel bans, and in egregious cases, attach the directors' personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement customer due diligence on cross-border suppliers and buyers, failing to file suspicious and unusual transaction reports (STRs), or failing to report cash transactions above the regulatory threshold (e.g., R24,999.99 under FICA) when processing matcha trade payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) 38 of 2001, a person who fails to comply with the reporting and record-keeping duties may be liable for a fine of up to R10 million and/or imprisonment for up to 15 years. Corporate penalties may also be imposed alongside individual liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers who were aware of or condoned the failure to report, or who facilitated the laundering of trade proceeds, face direct criminal liability, including imprisonment, travel bans, extradition, and personal fines. Civil liability may also include compensation to affected parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting an artificially low sale price for matcha imported from a foreign affiliate, or paying excess royalties or management fees to a related company, thereby eroding South African taxable income and shifting profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS will adjust the taxable income to be consistent with the arm's length standard. An understatement penalty of up to 200% may be imposed depending on the taxpayer's conduct, plus prescribed interest on the additional tax from the original due date. Repeated non-compliance may be treated as fraudulent and lead to criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve significant related-party transactions and sign off on tax returns may be personally liable for the assessed shortfall if found negligent or reckless. Personal liability may include payment of the full additional tax, penalties, and interest, and in cases of deliberate fraud, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to submit the ITR14 or the provisional tax returns (IRP6) by the statutory deadlines, or failing to pay the assessed corporate income tax when due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of up to R250 per month for each month of non-compliance, capped at R4,000 per tax year. Late payment of tax attracts a 10% late-payment penalty plus statutory interest at the prescribed rate. SARS may block tax clearance, attach bank accounts, seize assets, or apply for the company to be wound up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts under section 237 of the Tax Administration Act if the company is liquidated due to negligence or if they are involved in the failure to file or pay. A court may also suspend directors' ability to act in management, impose travel bans, and in egregious cases order imprisonment.
